gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'We've been waiting for hours,' the passengers complained. The passengers complained that they ___ waiting for hours.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been waiting → had been waiting after the past reporting verb 'complained'.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
gaps.explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave the building immediately!' the firefighter ordered. The firefighter ordered us ___ the building immediately.
gaps.explanation: Orders are reported with order + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Please, please help me,' the woman begged. The woman begged ___ her.
gaps.explanation: Begging is reported as beg + somebody + to do something.
